newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Japanese firms near deal on Natuna stake-Pertamina.
newsitem.headline: Japanese firms near deal on Natuna stake-Pertamina.

text.p: Indonesia's state oil company Pertamina said on Wednesday a consortium of Japanese firms were close to an agreement on acquiring a stake in the giant Natuna gas project in the South China Sea.

"I have met with officials of Indonesia Petroleum Ltd (INPEX) of Japan who informed me the Japanese consortium is eager to participate in the Natuna project," Pertamina's president director Faisal Abda'oe told reporters.
"They are close to reaching an agreement on participating in the Natuna project," he said.
He said Pertamina, which has 24 percent stake in Natuna, plans to reduce its share to 11 percent. Mobil Corp has 26 percent and Exxon Corp 50 percent in the project.
"The Japanese firms are expected to take 13 percent," he said.
Pertamina general affair director Baharuddin said in December the consortium included Nissho Iwai Corp, Mitsubishi Corp, Mitsui and Co Ltd and INPEX.
The Natuna field is estimated to contain 210 trillion cubic feet (Tcf) of gas, of which 45 Tcf are thought to be recoverable commercially .
